name: Outdoors
description: Birds at dawn, crickets, a frog pond, a stream, distant thunder and wind chimes, synthesised live: hold a key to open the scene, more keys layer more of it, and the key's pitch tunes what is pitched.

params.name: Type
params.description: Which scene plays: songbirds at dawn, a field of crickets, frogs across a pond, a running stream, a distant thunderstorm or wind chimes tuned to the keys you hold.

params.name: Density
params.description: How much is going on: how many birds, crickets or frogs are calling and how often, how fast the water runs, how often thunder rolls or the chimes are struck.

params.name: Distance
params.description: How far away the scene is. Near is bright, dry and distinct; far is duller, softer at the edges and more uneven in level, as if heard across a field.

params.name: Movement
params.description: How much the scene changes over time: gusts in the chimes, waves of activity among the animals, surges in the stream. Turned right down, the scene holds steady.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Colour of the scene, from dark and mellow to bright. The key's pitch leans it as well: low keys give bigger, lower creatures and deeper water.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long the scene takes to fade in when a key is pressed.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long the scene takes to fade out after the key is released.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the sources spread across the stereo field. Fully open, every creature and chime has its own place; fully closed, the scene folds to mono.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many keys stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit: six procedural scenes, no recordings. Birds are chirped tones with a little breath, arranged by a phrase grammar; crickets are pulsed tones; frogs are pulse trains through formant resonators; thunder is many delayed and filtered arrivals of noise; chimes are the struck partials of a free-free bar: procedural audio after the approach of Farnell, 'Designing Sound'. The stream is a population of bubbles, damped sines whose pitch rises as they decay, after the approach of van den Doel, 'Physically Based Models for Liquid Sounds'. No constants were taken from either: the values here were set from measurements of the device's own output.
